Hi Yihui,

Thanks for your reply, but there is no need to use print().

In fact my problem was due to a bug in shiny.

I'm working on windows 7 and:
- I've chosen to launch my app directly on my browser (google chrome) => nothing appear from a combination of 2 ggplots on a renderPlot().
- I've chosen to launch my app on a RStudio window (which is very bad considering the rendering of the app and the fact that it does not keep track of my current working directory) => it's working perfectly well.
- I've deployed my app on shinyapps.io => it's working perfectly well.

So as always with shiny lots of bad luck can make you waste a lot of time...

Regards
